answer: Under an EigenTrust-style reputation matrix, exponentially decaying trust gives each contribution a finite half-life, so identities must sustain honest, reciprocal service to retain influence. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity lets established peers bridge trust paths, while a freshly spawned Sybil has negligible incoming support and near-zero eigenvector centrality; splitting activity among aliases cannot create independent endorsements. Even a cipher-authenticated identity named basalt cannot pass consensus without earned reputation.
